page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at the top, page number at the top right. Gathering signature "B 3" at the foot. Catchword "tinea" at the bottom right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: Peccant igitur grauissimè contra puritatem verbi Dei illi, qui ostentanda nescio cuius eruditionis gratia, è suggestis varia profanorum, Philosophorum, Poetarum etiam obscoenorum dicta non solum citant, sed etiam integra recitant atq; explicant.

Non me latet, Apostolum Paulum nonnun-quam in suis sermonibus & Epistolis, profanorum etiam Poetarum dicta, quòd ad rem, quam tractabat, essent accommodata, citasse: ut in Actis illud Arati, τοῦ γὰρ καὶ γένος ἐσμέν [?]: ut in 1. (cor. ιε [?]. illud Menandri, φθείρουσιν ἤθη χρηστὰ ὁμιλίαι κακαί [?]: ut in epist. ad Titum, c. 1. illud Epimenidis, Κρῆτες ἀεὶ ψεῦσται, κακὰ θηρία, γαστέρες ἀργαί.

Verum, neq; nominauit Poetas, neq; id fecit frequenter, neq; sine utili causa: sed breuiatantum illorum dicta, raro, sobrie, & quasi obiter, coactus adduxit: ut qui erant ex gentibus, ipsorum quoq; Gentilium dictis, quasi propriis confode-rentur armis. Quid igitur hoc Apostoli exemplum iuuat illos, qui citra ullam necessitatem, aut etiam utilitatem, tantùm ut ostentent nescio quam vanam eruditionem, assuefaciunt mentes fidelium audiendis multorum eruditorum hominum testimoniis? Solus Christus in Ecclesia audiendus est, si volumus puram eius doctrinam in Ecclesia conseruari. Hanc priorem regulam docuit nos Apostolus in altera ad Timoth. epist. cap 2. Quæ audiuisti (inquiens) ex me, inter multos testes: hæc propone fidelibus hominibus, qui erunt ἱκανοὶ, καὶ ἑτέρους διδάξαι [?], nempe eadem, & non alia: quasi dicat, Et ita nostrare-

page.notes: Greek passages are read from a slightly blurred scan; the accents and breathings of the Arati, Menandri and 2 Tim. 2:2 quotations are uncertain and marked [?]. The "ιε" beside "1. (cor." is probably a printed chapter number, read as Greek numeral; the reference is uncertain. The word at the line end "nostrare-" continues on the catchword "tinea" and is unresolved. Line-end marks after "puritatem", "obscoenorum" and similar words are read as plain line ends, not hyphens. Printed spellings such as "neq;", "quoq;", "breuiatantum", "audiuisti" and "coactus" are kept as printed; u/v were normalised only where a vowel or consonant was clear.
